title: Factor an fs monoid injection through its Kummer saturation
statement:
Let $P,Q$ be fine saturated commutative monoids [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], written additively, and let $h:P\to Q$ induce an injective group homomorphism $h^{\rm gp}:P^{\rm gp}\to Q^{\rm gp}$. Set $C=Q^{\rm gp}/h^{\rm gp}(P^{\rm gp})$ and suppose its torsion subgroup $C_{\rm tor}=\{c\in C:\exists n\geq1,\ nc=0\}$ is finite. Define
$$R=\{q\in Q:\exists n\geq1,\ nq\in h(P)\},\qquad H=\{g\in Q^{\rm gp}:\exists n\geq1,\ ng\in h^{\rm gp}(P^{\rm gp})\}.$$
Then $R$ is a fine saturated submonoid of $Q$, and its group completion identifies with $H$. The map $h$ factors as $P\xrightarrow{a}R\xrightarrow{b}Q$, with $a(p)=h(p)$ and $b$ the inclusion. Both group maps are injective, $H/h^{\rm gp}(P^{\rm gp})=C_{\rm tor}$ canonically, and $Q^{\rm gp}/H$ is torsion free. Every $r\in R$ has a positive multiple in $a(P)$; this condition together with injectivity is the meaning of Kummer here. Thus the cokernel of $a^{\rm gp}$ has order $\#C_{\rm tor}$ and is annihilated by that positive integer. No sharpness or torsion-freeness of $P^{\rm gp}$ or $Q^{\rm gp}$ is assumed.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.17, printed p.101 (root saturation); VI 2.1, printed p.71 (Kummer condition). This finite-index ambient-group factorization is agent supplied, not a quotation of VI 1.8. The intended proof uses lem-trf-fine-monoid-finite-saturation and is recorded in report.md.

proof.text: Write $G=Q^{\rm gp}$ and $A=h^{\rm gp}(P^{\rm gp})$. By [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], $P$ and $Q$ embed in their group completions. The assumed injectivity of $h^{\rm gp}$ lets us identify $P$ with $h(P)\subseteq Q\subseteq G$ and $P^{\rm gp}$ with $A=P-P$. We use these identifications only in this proof. The set $H$ is a subgroup containing $A$: if $nx\in A$ and $my\in A$ with $n,m>0$, then $nm(x-y)=m(nx)-n(my)\in A$.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.17, printed p.101; agent-supplied ambient-group root-closure argument.

proof.text: The quotient map $G\to C=G/A$ sends $g$ to a torsion element exactly when $ng\in A$ for some $n>0$, that is, exactly when $g\in H$. Thus $g+A\mapsto g+A$ identifies $H/A$ bijectively and additively with $C_{\rm tor}$; its kernel before quotienting is $A$. Also $G/H$ is torsion free: if $k(g+H)=0$ with $k>0$, then $kg\in H$, so some $m>0$ has $mkg\in A$, hence $g\in H$ and $g+H=0$.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.17, printed p.101; agent-supplied ambient-group root-closure argument.

proof.text: The set $R$ contains $P$ and $0$ and is closed under addition: from $nr\in P$ and $ms\in P$ obtain $nm(r+s)=m(nr)+n(ms)\in P$. It is integral as a submonoid of $G$. In fact it is root closed in $G$: if $kg\in R$ with $g\in G$ and $k>0$, first $kg\in Q$ implies $g\in Q$ by the saturation clause of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]; next some $n>0$ has $nkg\in P$, proving $g\in R$. In particular $R$ is saturated in its own group completion once that completion is identified with its generated subgroup in $G$.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.17, printed p.101; agent-supplied ambient-group root-closure argument.

proof.text: Every element of $R$ belongs to $H$, so the subgroup $R-R$ is contained in $H$. Conversely let $g\in H$. Write $ng=p_1-p_2$ with $n>0$ and $p_1,p_2\in P$, using $A=P-P$. Then $n(g+p_2)=p_1+(n-1)p_2\in P\subseteq Q$. Saturation of $Q$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] gives $g+p_2\in Q$, and the same displayed equation gives $g+p_2\in R$. Since $p_2\in R$, we have $g=(g+p_2)-p_2\in R-R$. Hence $R-R=H$. The map $R^{\rm gp}\to G$ is injective with this image: every group-completion element is $r-s$, and equality $r-s=r^{\prime}-s^{\prime}$ in $G$ is $r+s^{\prime}=r^{\prime}+s$ in the submonoid $R$, which is precisely the equality of these fractions in $R^{\rm gp}$.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.17, printed p.101; agent-supplied ambient-group root-closure argument.

proof.text: By Step 2 the quotient $H/A$ is finite. Each of its classes has a representative in $R$: for any representative $g\in H$, the construction in Step 4 replaces it by $g+p_2\in R$ without changing its class modulo $A$. Choose such representatives $r_1,\ldots,r_t$. Let $M\subseteq H$ be the monoid generated by $P$ and these finitely many elements. A finite generating set of $P$ together with the $r_i$ generates $M$, and $P\subseteq M\subseteq R$. Its generated subgroup is $H$: for $g\in H$ choose $r_i$ in its class, so $g-r_i\in A=P-P\subseteq M-M$, and thus $g\in M-M$. As in Step 4, $M^{\rm gp}$ identifies with this subgroup. No assertion that an arbitrary submonoid of a fine monoid is fine has been used.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.17, printed p.101; agent-supplied ambient-group root-closure argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-fine-monoid-finite-saturation] to $M$: it is finitely generated by Step 5, integral because it is a submonoid of $H$, and its own group completion is $H$. The cited statement allows torsion in that group. It gives finite generation of $M^{\rm sat}=\{g\in H:\exists n>0,\ ng\in M\}$. This saturation equals $R$. Indeed $r\in R$ has a positive multiple in $P\subseteq M$, hence lies in $M^{\rm sat}$; conversely $ng\in M\subseteq R$ implies $g\in R$ by Step 3. Consequently $R$ is finitely generated; together with Step 3 this proves that it is fine saturated.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.17, p.101, and finite-saturation input of VIII 3.2.9, proof, p.104; applied to the finite monoid M in its own group H.

proof.text: Return to the original notation. Set $a(p)=h(p)$ with codomain $R$, which is well defined since $h(P)\subseteq R$, and let $b:R\to Q$ be inclusion. They are monoid homomorphisms and $b\circ a=h$. Under $R^{\rm gp}=H\subseteq Q^{\rm gp}$ from Step 4, $a^{\rm gp}$ is $h^{\rm gp}$ with codomain restricted to $H$, and $b^{\rm gp}$ is inclusion. Thus both are injective and their cokernels are $H/h^{\rm gp}(P^{\rm gp})\cong C_{\rm tor}$ and $Q^{\rm gp}/H$, respectively. Step 2 proves the latter torsion free. Every $r\in R$ has a positive multiple in $a(P)$ by the definition of $R$; together with injectivity this is exactly the Kummer condition specified in the statement.

source.place: Expose VI 2.1, printed p.71, Kummer condition; ambient-group factorization supplied by the agent.

proof.text: Let $N=\#C_{\rm tor}$. This is a positive integer because $C_{\rm tor}$ is a finite group containing zero. For $c\in C_{\rm tor}$, translation $t\mapsto c+t$ permutes the finite set $C_{\rm tor}$. Summing in the abelian group $C$ gives $\sum_t t=\sum_t(c+t)=Nc+\sum_t t$, hence $Nc=0$ by cancellation. The canonical identification in Step 2 transfers both cardinality $N$ and annihilation by $N$ to the cokernel of $a^{\rm gp}$. This includes $C_{\rm tor}=0$, for which $N=1$.

source.place: Expose VI 2.1--2.2, pp.71--72, finite cokernel annihilator requirement; elementary finite-group summation argument.
